Sasha: FYI ran the nightly continuous-batching perf job after the kernel-selector change, and we're seeing steady GPU memory growth + a small latency regression on pool-3.
Sasha: Quick summary: +12% p95 tokens, OOMs on a few 32GB machines with mixed seq workloads.
Marc: ugh. timeline? did the kernel switch rollout map to pool-3 yesterday? @infra-bot?
infra-bot: deploy: kernel-selector v1.9 rolled to pool-3 at 2026-03-15T03:20Z :rocket:
Sasha: repro attached below — profiler snippet from the job (trimmed):
```
profiler.summary {
  batches: 1824
  avg_batch_size: 7.3
  avg_seq_len: 114
  pad_waste_pct: 21.7
  gpu_mem_peak: 73.4GB
  kv_cache_resident: 8.2GB
  workspace_alloc_peak: 12.7GB
  kernel_chosen: attention_fast_mem_opt (switch v1.9)
}
```
Marc: pad_waste 21% with avg_seq 114 seems high, but not catastrophic. workspace_alloc_peak 12.7GB stands out.
Ani: my guess: the new kernel chooses a faster algorithm that allocates larger temp buffers per sequence (per-step workspace), and continuous-batcher growth isn't accounting for the per-seq workspace correctly.
Leo: can you paste a short example of the workspace footprint per token? also any allocator fragmentation numbers?
Sasha: short sample from one trace (seqs: [12,64,128,256])
```
step 0 -> workspace_req=1.2MB per-seq
step 1 -> workspace_req=4.8MB per-seq (for seq>64 kernel path)
step 2 -> cumulative_workspace=~9.6MB per-batch
slab_frag: 4.1GB
```
ops-oncall: seeing OOM alerts at 03:50 UTC on pool-3 for route /chat/generate, a few retries succeeded after fallback to kernel v1.8
Marc: So fallback helps. That implies fallback model/kernel route is lower-memory but slightly slower.
Ani: Proposed short-term mitigations:
- pin kernel-selector to prefer memory-efficient kernel for seq<128 on pool-3
- reduce reserved workspace slab size from 16GB -> 12GB for canary hosts (to force quicker reclaim)
- enable buffer-reuse heuristic in allocator (env REDWOOD_ALLOC_REUSE=1) for canary
Marc: Longer term we need continuous-batching accounting changes: track 'workspace_per_seq' separately and let the batch growth ledger compute an upper bound rather than using avg_batch_size * avg_seq * single_workspace.
Sasha: I sketched a ledger change last night. Pseudocode:
```
// on batch enqueue
batch.workspace_account += max_per_seq_workspace(seq_len)
// on kernel route switch
if chosen_kernel.memory_profile > queued_kernel_profile:
  reserve_extra = chosen_kernel.per_seq_work * queued_batch_size
  trigger_rebalance_or_fallback()
```
Leo: also add kv-cache shadowing check: if KV cache residency grows during long tail requests, that steals allocator space. add a soft-limit alarm when kv_cache_resident > 70% of slab.
ops-oncall: note — several of the OOMs were correlated with long chat sessions using reranking which pins large KV entries; better to evict small-ttl keys earlier.
Ani: I'm going to spin a canary on two nodes with REDWOOD_ALLOC_REUSE=1 and kernel-selector config lowered for seq<128. I'll also flip on detailed mem telemetry (per-step workspace histograms).
Sasha: thanks. For rollback plan, infra-bot scheduled a quick flag flip; Marc can you prepare a canary checklist? items: heap profile collection, KV residency snapshot, roll-forward, monitor p95 tokens, and necessary alarms.
Marc: yep. I'll add canary checklist to the runbook and set alerts: slab_free < 2GB or pad_waste > 30% or p95_tokens +10%.
infra-bot: job created: canary-kernel-balance-180999 at 2026-03-15T05:00Z
Sasha: after canary we should also run a synthetic mixed-seq replay (50k requests) with both old and new kernel paths to quantify pad waste vs workspace delta.
Leo: quick diagnostic command for tracing per-step allocs:
```
rdw-infer --trace-allocs --route /chat/generate --samples 5000 > alloc-trace.log
```
Sasha: OK starting canary in 5m. I'll attach alloc-trace and profiler dumps to the canary issue.
ops-oncall: ping me if OOMs spike in prod, I'll throttle incoming traffic and flip fallback.
Marc: great. follow-up: we should update model-kernel metadata to include per-seq memory curves so selector can pick memory-safe kernels under memory pressure.
Ani: yep adding that to roadmap item: kernel-memory-curves + selector policy tiering.
Sasha: closing loop here, will post results in this thread when canary completes. :thumbsup:
